answer: The warden passes his brass ring through every net before it may be set in the loch, and the mesh size is written in the fishing book with the fisherman's name. A forge net woven with a finer mesh fails the ring: the signal of the loch must hold fish of the size the book allows, and a fine net takes the young ones. Forging the catch means weaving nets for a season, fishing 90 nights and paying 7,200, while the glacier entry in the fishing book is read at every landing, so a net whose mesh was never gauged is burned on the shore.
